page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine configuration powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8581C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The instance allocates 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU subsystem includes 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache, alongside specialized instruction sets including AVX-512 (with VNNI and BF16 extensions) and Intel AMX (tile and int8) for matrix acceleration.

System memory consists of 60.0 GB of RAM, providing 3.75 GB per vCPU. The instance comes without bundled local storage and features zero GPUs, requiring remote block storage for persistent disk access. Benchmark evaluations reveal standout single-threaded performance, with Geekbench single-core testing reaching top-tier levels at 2269.0 points and text processing scoring 3070.0 points. Data compression tasks similarly perform in the top 25% bracket, registering 35.06 GB/sec on single-threaded gzip and 14.89 GB/sec on single-threaded bzip3 decompression.

Under multi-threaded stress and broader system evaluations, performance aligns with middle-tier expectations. The instance achieved 14602.98 in stress-ng multi-core tests, a PassMark CPU score of 23179.01, and Redis throughput of 24.75 million SET operations per second. Memory throughput reached 109.68 GB/sec on uncached read operations and 50.45 GB/sec on write operations. Small-model LLM generation (135M parameters) demonstrated strong throughput at 330.39 tokens per second.

The c4-standard-16 maintains a balanced compute-to-memory profile suitable for general-purpose workloads, enterprise web serving, compilation environments, caching nodes, and light machine learning inference. The absence of local disk requires external persistent storage, making it ideal for stateless web services and containerized workloads rather than high-IOPS local database hosting.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-16 is a general-purpose virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 60.0 GB of memory running on an Intel Xeon 8581C x86_64 processor at 2.3 GHz across 8 physical cores. The instance incorporates advanced vector and matrix acceleration instructions, including AVX-512 and Intel AMX, alongside a 260 MB L3 cache. It does not include local disk storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on attached persistent network volumes. Benchmark evaluations show top-tier single-core efficiency, notable in Geekbench single-core results and single-threaded gzip compression, while multi-core metrics and uncached memory bandwidth align with mid-range general-purpose expectations. Yielding 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU, the c4-standard-16 delivers reliable throughput for static web serving, enterprise application backends, software compilation pipelines, caching layers, and lightweight CPU-based model inference.
